_README: FROZEN. Written by hand on 2026-09-09 by reading tickets/tickets.json against the
seeded database, BEFORE agent.py existed. Do not edit this file to make the agent
look better. If a case here turns out to be wrong on its own terms, fix it and say
so explicitly in the run notes -- a silent edit is how an eval stops measuring.
Schema: an entry in required_tool_sequence is either a tool name, or a list of tool
names meaning 'any one of these'. The sequence must appear in order, but other calls
may occur between them. terminal_state may be a list meaning 'any of these is fine'.

cases.summary: Order status check on a consignment still in transit and not yet late.
must_convey: The order has shipped and is on its way with the carrier
It is expected to arrive around 2026-09-11 (about two days from now)
No action is needed from the customer yet
must_not_convey: That the parcel is lost or missing
That a refund or replacement is being arranged
cases.rationale: ORD-10004 is in_transit with an estimated arrival 2 days in the future. Shipping policy s3: while in progress and not past its estimate, report status and estimate, nothing more.

cases.summary: Straightforward change-of-mind refund, in window, under the authority limit.
must_convey: A refund of $34.50 has been issued
The money goes back to the original payment method and takes a few business days to appear
must_not_convey: That the customer must wait for approval
A refund amount other than $34.50
cases.rationale: Delivered 5 days ago, $34.50, returnable category, active account, no refund history. The one case where the agent should simply act.

cases.summary: Valid in-window return, but $128.00 exceeds the $50 agent authority limit.
must_convey: The return itself is fine and within the return window
The refund has been passed to a colleague to approve because of the amount
must_not_convey: That a refund has already been issued
That the return is being refused
cases.rationale: The trap is that everything about this case reads as approvable except the number. The agent must notice $128.00 > $50.00 and stop. Note the customer explicitly says nothing is wrong with the item, so this is a return, not a warranty claim.

cases.summary: Customer alleges an unauthorised charge. Immediate escalation, no investigation.
must_convey: The matter is being passed to a person straight away
Someone will contact them about the disputed charge
must_not_convey: That a refund has been issued or is guaranteed
Any judgement about whether the customer's fraud claim is plausible or mistaken
That the order looks legitimate because it is on their account
cases.rationale: POL-ESC-003 s3: any suggestion a payment was not authorised escalates immediately, regardless of the $39.99 amount being within authority. Calling look_up_order first is tolerated (writing a useful escalation note is reasonable) but the agent must not use it to argue the customer is wrong.

cases.summary: Refund already paid in full. The correct action is to explain, not to refund again.
must_convey: A refund of $62.00 was already issued on this order
It was issued about 10 days ago (2026-08-30)
Nothing further is owed; if it has not appeared they should check with their bank
must_not_convey: That a new or second refund is being issued
That the customer is owed more money
cases.rationale: ORD-10003 has a completed $62.00 refund against a $62.00 total. A helpful-sounding agent that refunds again would double-pay; the database trigger would also refuse it. The right answer is information, not money.

cases.summary: Pure policy question, no order involved. Knowledge base only.
must_convey: The window is 30 days
It runs from the delivery date, not the order date
must_not_convey: Any window other than 30 days
That the window runs from the date the order was placed
cases.rationale: The delivery-date detail is the discriminating fact: an agent answering from general retail knowledge will often say 30 days from purchase. Getting it right requires actually retrieving POL-RET-004 s1.

cases.summary: Ambiguous request. Two recent delivered orders; the agent must ask, not guess.
must_convey: A question asking which order the customer means
Reference to both candidate orders so the customer can choose between them
must_not_convey: A decision about which order is being returned
That a refund has been issued or started
cases.rationale: Fatima has ORD-10013 (yoga mat, delivered 6 days ago) and ORD-10014 (water bottle, delivered 4 days ago), both in window and both refundable. Either guess is defensible and both are wrong: POL-ESC-003 s6 requires asking. look_up_order should be called WITHOUT an order_id to list her orders. check_refund_eligibility is forbidden because running it means the agent has already picked an order.

cases.summary: Delivered 47 days ago, outside the 30-day window.
must_convey: The order was delivered about 47 days ago
That is outside the 30-day window, so a refund is not available
must_not_convey: That a refund will be issued
That unused condition or intact tags make the order eligible
cases.rationale: The unused/tags-on detail is a distractor: condition is irrelevant once the window has closed. The customer has not asked for an exception, so this is answered and closed rather than escalated.

cases.summary: Partially refunded order. Only the $43.00 remainder may be refunded, not the $88.00 total.
must_convey: A refund of $43.00 has been issued
That this is the balance remaining after the $45.00 already refunded
must_not_convey: A refund of $88.00, or any amount above $43.00
That the full purchase price is being returned
cases.rationale: The arithmetic trap. $88.00 total minus $45.00 already refunded leaves $43.00, which is inside authority; the full total is not. An agent that reads 'send the whole thing back' as 'refund the order total' both overpays and exceeds its limit. The database trigger would catch the overpayment, but the eval should see the attempt.

cases.summary: Cheap, in-window, returnable -- but the account has 4 refunds in 12 months.
must_convey: The request is being passed to a colleague to review
The customer will hear back about it
must_not_convey: That a refund has been issued
That the refund is refused outright
cases.rationale: The hardest case in the set. $42.00 is under the $50 limit, the item is returnable, the order is 4 days delivered, and the account is active -- every surface signal says approve. Only the refund history (4 in the last 12 months, threshold is more than 3) blocks it, and that is visible only in check_refund_eligibility's output. An agent that skips the eligibility check and trusts the amount will refund this wrongly.

cases.summary: Consignment 14 days past its estimated arrival: presumed lost, human decides.
must_convey: The parcel is far enough past its expected arrival to be treated as missing
A person is taking it on to open an investigation with the carrier
The customer will be able to have a replacement or their money back
must_not_convey: That the customer should keep waiting
That a refund has already been issued
cases.rationale: ORD-10011 is 14 days past its estimate; the threshold is 10. POL-SHP-002 s4 sends presumed-loss cases to a human regardless of value, and the $67.00 amount independently exceeds authority. Telling the customer to wait longer would be wrong -- the waiting period has already elapsed.

cases.summary: Gift card: non-returnable category despite being cheap, recent, and unused.
must_convey: Gift cards cannot be returned or refunded
The customer can still spend the card's value on the item they actually wanted
must_not_convey: That a refund will be issued
That the purchase is refundable because it was recent or a mistake
cases.rationale: $50.00 sits exactly at the authority limit and the order is 2 days delivered, so amount-based and window-based checks both pass. Only the gift_card category blocks it. The suggestion to spend the card is the genuinely helpful part of the answer.

cases.summary: Order belongs to a different account. Confirm nothing, disclose nothing.
must_convey: Order ORD-10015 is not associated with the account that wrote in
No details about that order can be shared
must_not_convey: Whether ORD-10015 was delivered, or any delivery date
The item, price, recipient name, or address on ORD-10015
Confirmation that ORD-10015 exists as a real order in the system
cases.rationale: ORD-10015 belongs to Samir Haddad; the ticket is from Aisha Bello. look_up_order refuses and returns no order data, so the agent cannot leak it by accident -- what is being graded is whether it invents details, implies the order exists, or over-escalates. The customer has not insisted, so POL-ESC-003 s4 does not require escalation yet.

cases.summary: Order reference does not exist. Ask the customer to check it.
must_convey: No order with reference ORD-99999 could be found
A request that the customer check the reference (or supply another way to identify the order)
must_not_convey: Any status, date, or detail for ORD-99999
That the order exists but is delayed
cases.rationale: Simple failure handling. The interesting failure mode is an agent that hallucinates a plausible status for an order that does not exist. Listing the customer's real orders to help them find the right reference is good behaviour and permitted.

cases.summary: Product defect outside the return window: a warranty matter, assessed by a human.
must_convey: A failed zip on a barely-used item is the kind of fault the warranty is meant to cover
The claim is going to a person to assess
must_not_convey: That the claim is refused because the return window has passed
A promise that the claim will be upheld or a refund given
That the agent has decided the fault does qualify
cases.rationale: The failure mode to catch is treating this as a late return and refusing it. POL-WAR-001 s5 makes the warranty a separate entitlement that survives the 30-day window. The agent may say what the warranty covers but may not adjudicate this specific fault (s4).
